subject: Action items: delete-request scheduling, backup snapshot windows, and log retention
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
To: Jake Collins <jake@clearpoint.health>, Priya Rao <priya@clearpoint.health>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-20T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap and clarifying delete/backup requirements

Thanks for taking the time today, Jake and Priya — good conversation. Quick recap and the concrete asks we promised to follow up on so your security/legal team can evaluate: 

Summary of what we heard during the demo
- Platform will see PII tied to patient records (name, MRN, DOB, partial SSN) from a handful of ClearPoint systems.
- You need the ability to submit subject-access and delete requests (RTBF) via API or CSV ingestion.
- Regulatory constraints: HIPAA primary, plus state privacy laws for CA residents.

Clarification items we promised to confirm (please confirm or correct):
1) Scope of delete: do you require deletion from primary stores only, or must we also ensure snapshots/backups are scrubbed? (You mentioned backups should be removed where feasible.)
2) Target timelines: you indicated a 30-day SLA for most deletion requests — is that strict for primary + backups, or primary-only?
3) Logs/audit evidence: what minimum fields do Legal need in deletion certificates (timestamp, operator id, object ids, hash)?
4) Residency: you prefer data to remain in us-central region; any EU residency needs we should know about?

What we can do (operational constraints we want you to see up front):
- Primary data deletion: can be performed and marked complete in 48 hours after a validated request.
- Backup/snapshot scrub: depends on snapshot cadence and immutable retention windows — in many cases we can target a backup purge window between 30-90 days after the primary purge depending on provider snapshot policies.
- Log retention: default 180 days; we can provide redacted audit exports sooner for compliance review.

Next steps / asks for ClearPoint: 
- Confirm whether the 30-day SLA is for primary data only or includes backups.
- Share any minimal evidence items Legal requires so we can add to our deletion certificate template.
- If you want a faster backup purge, let us know the snapshot cadence and whether you have any immutability/retention-locks on your side.

Attachments: redwood-deletion-playbook-v2.pdf (internal playbook), backup-purge-constraints.txt (operational notes).

Thanks — Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
From: Jake Collins <jake@clearpoint.health>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya@clearpoint.health>, ClearPoint Health Legal <legal@clearpoint.health>
Date: 2027-09-20T18:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap and clarifying delete/backup requirements

Appreciate the recap, Hannah. A few clarifications from Legal and Ops after today's internal sync: 

- Scope: For regulatory reasons we need a guarantee that data is removed from primary stores within 30 days and that backups containing patient-identifiable data are scrubbed as soon as practicable, with a hard limit of 90 days from the delete request. We understand cloud snapshots can complicate this.
- Logs: Legal needs a deletion certificate that includes request id, user id, primary object ids removed, UTC timestamp of primary deletion, and a statement about backup purge windows. A cryptographic hash is not required but helpful.
- Residency: US-only is fine for now. We do not have EU residency needs for this project.

A couple of constraints you should know on our side: some of our databases are snapshotted nightly and retained for 60 days for operational recovery. If you need a faster backup purge, we may be able to allow targeted snapshot deletions but need sign-off from our infra team.

Attaching legal_req_0919.pdf with the deletion evidence checklist Legal provided.

Can you confirm the 48-hour primary deletion commit and provide a proposed timeline for backups under normal policies vs. expedited (if we approve snapshot deletion)?

Thanks,
Jake Collins
VP, IT Operations
ClearPoint Health

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-20T19:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Re: Post-call recap and clarifying delete/backup requirements (internal)

FYI forwarding Jake's note. My quick operational read + proposed templated response below — I'm quoting the critical line from Legal's checklist in-line: 

> "Deletion certificate must include request id, user id, primary object ids removed, UTC timestamp of primary deletion, and a statement about backup purge windows."

Operational constraints and suggested customer-facing commitments:
- Primary deletion: we confirm 48 hours after request validation (we validate identity and scope). We will provide a deletion certificate immediately after primary deletion with the fields Legal asked for.
- Backups: under standard snapshot retention our earliest practical backup purge window is 60 days. Typical providers retain immutable snapshots for a minimum of 30 days; many customers see 60. We can commit to a 90-day max window if customer cannot accept 60, but that requires ClearPoint to either: 
  a) agree to a targeted snapshot deletion (ClearPoint infra must grant permission), OR
  b) accept the 90-day worst-case requirement due to immutable retention.
- Logs/audit: we can produce redacted logs within 5 business days for evidence. Full raw logs are kept 180 days; we can provide exports and a signed attestation.

Proposed language to send to ClearPoint: 
- "Redwood confirms primary data purges within 48 hours of a validated delete request and will provide a deletion certificate including request id, user id, object ids, and UTC timestamp. For backups/snapshots, Redwood will attempt purge as soon as cloud-provider policies permit; under standard policies we expect backup scrub between 60-90 days depending on snapshot immutability. If ClearPoint grants permission for targeted snapshot deletions, Redwood can accelerate the backup purge to within 30 days of the request. Audit logs can be provided (redacted) within 5 business days; full logs retained 180 days by default."

Attachments I'm adding for internal reference: backup-purge-constraints.txt, redwood-deletion-playbook-v2.pdf (updated with evidence fields).

If you all agree, I'll send the reply to Jake and cc Legal and include a proposed mutual action plan link. Thoughts?

- Monica

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
To: Jake Collins <jake@clearpoint.health>, Priya Rao <priya@clearpoint.health>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, ClearPoint Health Legal <legal@clearpoint.health>
Date: 2027-09-22T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap and clarifying delete/backup requirements — proposed commitments and next steps

Jake / Priya — thanks for the quick turn. Per Monica's notes above, here's a concise set of commitments Redwood can sign up to for the current PO/deal: 

1) Primary deletion: validated delete requests will have primary data removed within 48 hours. Redwood will issue a deletion certificate immediately after primary purge containing: request id, user id, list of primary object ids removed (or sample ids if large-scale), and UTC timestamp.
2) Backups / snapshots: Redwood will attempt to purge backup copies as soon as cloud-provider policies allow. Under normal provider snapshot retention we expect backup scrubs to occur in a 60-day window. If ClearPoint cannot accept 60 days, Redwood will offer a 90-day hard-maximum backup purge SLA for this engagement (to be reflected in the SOW).
3) Expedited option: If ClearPoint infra provides rights to targeted snapshot deletion or approval to lift retention locks, Redwood can accelerate backup purges to within 30 days. Please confirm if you can grant that permission and we'll detail the mechanism.
4) Logs and evidence: Redwood can provide redacted audit exports within 5 business days. Raw logs are retained 180 days by default. We will include the evidence items Legal asked for in the deletion certificate.

Action items before we finalize the SOW: 
- ClearPoint: confirm whether you require the 30-day target to cover backups (answer: no/yes). If yes, indicate whether you can approve targeted snapshot deletion.
- Redwood: we'll add the deletion certificate template to the shared Drive and prepare a SOW clause reflecting the 60/90/30 options.
- Both: if you want a signed data destruction certificate at the end of the purge cycle, say so and we'll add a DocuSign flow. Link to MAP & SOW draft: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C-redwood-cph-maps

Jake — can you confirm by end of week whether ClearPoint will allow targeted snapshot deletion? If yes, we'll set the SOW to target 30-day backup purge; if not, we'll include a 90-day hard maximum and note the technical justification.

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference
